VII.}}</noinclude>''2'', Where he checketh some of them for preferring them selues before Priests, and putteth them in remembrance of their first calling, that they be as the Leuites vvere in respect of the Priests of the old Law. finally by S. Ambrose ''li. 1 Offic. c. 41'' and Prudentius ''in Hymno de S. Laurent''. speaking of S. Laurence the Deacon, vve may see their Office vvas most holy. See S. Augustine also of the dignitie of Deacons ''ep. 148 ad Valerium. Conc. Carthag. 4. can. 37. 38. 39. 41''.

{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. VII.}}}}}}

{{c|''Steuen being permitted to ansvver, beginning at Abraham, shevveth that God was with their fathers both in other places, and also long before the Temple. 48 and that after it vvas built, it could not be (as they grosly imagined) a house for God to dvvel in. 51 then he inueigheth against their stifneckednes, and telleth them boldly of their traiterous murdering of Christ, as their fathers had done his Prophets afore him. 54 Whereat they being vvood, he seeth heauen open, and IESVS there in his Diuine Maiestie. 57 Whereat they become more mad, so that they stone him to death (Saul consenting) he commending his soul to IESVS, and humbly praying for them.''}} {{dropinitial|A|image=Rhemes New Testament 1582 initial A, scrolling foliage with grotesque heads.png|imgsize=140px|fl={{verse|chapter=7|verse=1}}}}ND the cheefe priest said, Are these things so? {{verse|chapter=7|verse=2}}† Vvho said, Ye men, brethren and fathers, heare. The God of glorie appeared to our father Abraham vvhen he vvas in Mesopotamia, before that he abode in Charan, {{verse|chapter=7|verse=3}}† and said to him, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Gen. 12, 1.''}}* ''Goe forth out of thy countrie, and out of thy kinred, and come into a land that I shal shevv thee''. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=4}}† Then vvent he forth out of the land of the Chaldees, and dvvelt in Charan. And from thence, after his father vvas dead, he translated him into this land, vvherein you doe novv dvvel. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=5}}† And he gaue him no inheritance in it, no not the pase of a foote: and he promised to giue it him in possession, and to his seede after him, vvhen as he had no childe. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=6}}† And God spake to him, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Gen. 15, 13.''}}* ''That his seede shal be a soiourner in a strange countrie, and they shal subdue them to seruitude, and shal euil intreate them foure-hundred yeres'': {{verse|chapter=7|verse=7}}† ''and the nation vvhich they shal serue, vvil I iudge'', said God. ''and after these things they shal goe forth, and '' {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''λατρεύσουσι.''}}∷ ''shal serue me in this place''.

{{verse|chapter=7|verse=8}}† And he {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Gen. 17.''}}* gaue him the testament of circumcision, and so he {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Gen. 21.''}}* begat Isaac, and circumcised him the eight day: and {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Gen. 25.''}}* Isaac, Iacob: and {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Gen. 29, 30. 35.''}}* Iacob, the tvvelue Patriarches. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=9}}† And the Patriarches through emulation, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Gen. 37.''}}* sold Ioseph into Ægypt. and God vvas vvith him: {{verse|chapter=7|verse=10}}† and deliuered him out of al his tribulations. and he {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Gen. 41.''}}* gaue him grace and vvisedom in the sight of Pharao the king of Ægypt, and he appointed him Gouernour ouer Ægypt and ouer al his house. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=11}}† And there came famin vpon al Ægypt and Chanaan, and great tribulation: and our fathers found no victuals. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=12}}† But vvhen {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Gen. 42.''}}* Iacob had heard that there vvas corne in Ægypt: he sent our<noinclude>{{rh|||fathers}}</noinclude>
